evidence: Report asserts: 'comfortably inside the 5% requirement, by approximately one standard error.'
The Upper Control Limit (UCL) for a p-chart with p-bar=0.0352 and n=200 is approximately 0.074 (7.4%), which is well above the 5% requirement.
A capability Z-score of 0.96 indicates the specification limit is less than one standard deviation away from the mean, meaning the target will frequently be missed.
rationale: The report fundamentally misinterprets process capability. While the long-term average (3.52%) is indeed below the 5% target, the process variation is too wide to consistently meet this target on a per-period basis. A capability Z-score of 0.96 means the process average is only ~1 standard error away from the maximum limit, representing very poor capability. Consequently, the natural variation (which extends to an Upper Control Limit of ~7.4%) will routinely cause individual periods to exceed 5%. Recommending to stop improvement, 'maintain' the process, and only investigate when the UCL is breached amounts to accepting routine failures against the business requirement.
numerical_check: Calculated p-chart UCL for p=0.0352, n=200: UCL = 0.0352 + 3*sqrt(0.0352*(1-0.0352)/200) = 0.0743. Calculated binomial capability Z for target 0.05, n=200, p=0.0352: Z = (0.05 - 0.0352) / sqrt(0.05*0.95/200) = 0.9603.
